note.question: Why might a firm deliberately assign the same price to products with different costs even when fine-grained pricing is technologically feasible?
note.overview: A multiproduct monopolist commits to prices, consumers form state-contingent reference plans before tastes are realized, and purchases must be optimal and internally consistent with those plans. The firm anticipates the resulting personal equilibria when choosing prices.

models.name: Monopoly price commitment with endogenous consumer reference points and personal equilibrium
models.summary: A multiproduct monopolist commits to prices, consumers form state-contingent reference plans before tastes are realized, and purchases must be optimal and internally consistent with those plans. The firm anticipates the resulting personal equilibria when choosing prices.

source.quote: Crawford and Meng (2011) find that drivers with expectations about wage and working hours stop working upon reaching anticipated target hours.

My research contributes to the literature examining firm strategies for loss-averse consumers/agents, which has addressed channel contracting (Ho and Zhang 2008), produce line design (Orhun 2009), dynamic price competition (Kuksov and Wang 2014), differentiated price competition (Amaldoss and He 2018), and quality disclosure (Zhang and Li 2021).

Although previous literature proposes firms’ costly price setting activities as a friction-based explanation, I offer a consumer-driven rationale rooted in reference-dependent and loss-averse consumer behaviors.
Class pricing describes a widespread practice of assigning a few price points to a large set of differentiated products.

models.method: The paper derives credible consumer plans under Kőszegi-Rabin expectations-based reference dependence, maps those plans to demand, solves the monopolist's constrained price problem first for two products, and extends the logic to N products and endogenous class sizes.

components.label: Price-commitment subgame with consumer personal equilibria
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Price-commitment subgame with consumer personal equilibria. A plan is a personal equilibrium when its prescribed choice maximizes ex post reference-dependent utility and satisfies participation for every taste state. Proposition 1 establishes the two-product subgame equilibrium, and the monopolist optimizes prices over the induced PE demand.
